solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Disclaimer which is must-see for ordering?

indicators.note: putting letters in order means rearranging them, so these clue letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A cinema poster disclaimer asks which film is the must-see one to order tickets for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordering' sits at the end posing as a noun about booking, but it rearranges MUST-SEE FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The conditions printed on a website or product often act as a legal disclaimer limiting liability.

clue.text: Pool worker starts to take you paddling in swimming trunks

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Someone at the pool takes you paddling in your swimming trunks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pool' is not a swimming pool but an office typing pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Typing pools were offices where secretarial staff did shared clerical keyboard work.

clue.text: Old actor, on once more, doesn't need one

parts.note: re means on, concerning

indicators.note: not needing a piece means it is dropped

parts.note: again means once more
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An old actor back on stage again, no longer needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald, later US President, was a Hollywood film star in his earlier career.

clue.text: Given new menus you all sit together

indicators.note: a new version of the letters is a rearranged one

explanation.surface: Diners handed fresh menus all sit down together.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things at the same time is doing them together, at one moment.

clue.text: Gift that's about to fill up trailer?

indicators.note: the gift 'that's' the other piece holds it inside

parts.note: a forte is a special talent or gift

indicators.note: about signals turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to sate is to fill up or satisfy

explanation.surface: A present that's about to fill up a trailer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns SATE into ETAS. 'trailer' is a film preview, not a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A film trailer gives a preview, an early sample of what is to come.

clue.text: Stage in flight where one's in the lead

indicators.note: one piece goes in another, inside it

parts.note: the star is the lead performer
one is I, the Roman numeral, with 's as is

explanation.surface: A stage during a flight where one is at the head of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' is a flight of steps, not travel by air.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of steps is made up of single steps, each one level.

clue.text: Fog causes problem crossing lake from far side

indicators.note: reading from the far side means the word is taken backwards
one piece crossing another stretches across it, so it is cut open to hold the other

parts.note: 'there's the rub' uses rub for a problem or snag
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Fog causes trouble for someone trying to cross a lake to the far shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' has RUB straddle L, giving RULB, and 'from far side' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A blur is an indistinct haze, as is a fog that obscures what lies ahead.

clue.text: Sue? Mark? It turned into romance

indicators.note: one piece goes into another, inside it

parts.note: to romance is to tell fanciful stories, to lie

indicators.note: turned means read backwards

parts.note: a tag is a label or mark

explanation.surface: Sue and Mark: it turned into a romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses TAG and IT together, giving TIGAT. Sue and Mark look like names; Sue is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue someone is to take them to court, bringing a lawsuit.

clue.text: Setting temperature in garden is an applied science

indicators.note: one piece set in another goes inside it

parts.note: a rockery is a garden of rocks and alpine plants

explanation.surface: Setting the right temperature in a garden is a practical science.
explanation.definitionFit: The design and launching of missiles and space vehicles is an engineering discipline.

clue.text: Evidence of harm dubious if string used to bind me

indicators.note: to bind something is to wrap around it, holding it inside
dubious means questionable, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: Dubious claims of harm if string was used to tie someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dubious' rearranges IF STRING USED, and 'to bind' has it wrap ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Scars and blemishes spoiling appearance are visible signs of injury.

clue.text: Hymn appropriate around beginning of service

indicators.note: one piece goes around another, holding it inside

parts.note: to palm something is to take it furtively, to appropriate it

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A hymn suited to the opening of a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' reads as an adjective but is the verb, to steal: PALM.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical psalms are sacred songs, a sort of religious hymn sung in worship.

clue.text: Sensible record covering very famous one

indicators.note: something covering another wraps around it, so it holds the other inside

parts.note: REC is a short form of record, as on a recorder's button
A-list describes the most famous celebrities
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sensible record cover features a very famous performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' looks like a disc but supplies only its abbreviation; A-list is the label for top-ranked celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sensible and down-to-earth means having a practical, pragmatic view of things.

clue.text: Try to eat complete onion

indicators.note: a piece eating another swallows it, holding it inside

parts.note: to have a shot is to make an attempt, a try
all means whole or complete

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to finish eating a whole onion.
explanation.definitionFit: This small mild bulb is a variety of onion used in cooking and pickling.

clue.text: Far from home, I am to fill up, mostly outside empty garage

indicators.note: one piece outside another surrounds it
mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: the order to fill up a tank again is to refuel

indicators.note: an empty word loses its contents, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A driver far from home needs to fill up but finds the garage empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts REFUEL to REFUE, which goes 'outside' GE, the shell of 'garage'.
explanation.definitionFit: A refugee has fled their country and is displaced, living far from where they belong.

clue.text: Chap's having hysterics on killing

parts.note: a chap is a man, so chap's gives man's
hysterics can mean uncontrollable fits of laughing

explanation.surface: A man laughs hysterically at something absolutely killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'killing' looks like slang for very funny, fitting the laughter, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlawful killing without premeditation is the legal crime so named.

clue.text: Nice feeling, possibly great, about initially feeling sad

indicators.note: being about another piece means going around it
possibly signals the letters could be arranged another way
initially means take the first letter

parts.note: low means sad or depressed

explanation.surface: A pleasant feeling that might be great, about first feeling sad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges GREAT to AFTERG around F.
explanation.definitionFit: The warm glow after a success or pleasant event is a lingering contentment.

clue.text: Not thinking properly / swallowing tablet?

indicators.note: one piece swallowing another takes it inside

parts.note: the printed stroke, the solidus, is also called a slash
a PDA, personal digital assistant, is a hand-held computer much like a tablet

explanation.surface: Someone careless takes a pill without a thought.
explanation.walkthrough: The stroke in the clue is itself wordplay: a solidus is called a slash. The question mark admits a PDA is not quite a tablet.
explanation.definitionFit: Hasty, careless work is done without proper thought or attention.

clue.text: Tree spreads if gardener cuts odd bits

indicators.note: cutting the odd letters leaves only the even-numbered ones

explanation.surface: A tree spreads if a gardener prunes odd branches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tree' is a family tree, not a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage or ancestry is set out in a family tree.

clue.text: Plastic electrode — it's for those picking up rubbish?

indicators.note: plastic means easily moulded into a new shape, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A plastic electrode used by litter pickers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish' here means untruths, and the machines pick up on lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Polygraphs detect falsehoods, and falsehoods are figuratively rubbish or nonsense.

clue.text: Boarding trains, it usually is not moved

indicators.note: boarding means getting on board, inside the words

explanation.surface: Boarding trains, it usually stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in its original place, left undisturbed.

clue.text: Avoid the online scene?

parts.note: E stands for electronic, as in e-mail, so online
a scape is a scene or view, as in landscape

explanation.surface: Avoid the internet scene?
explanation.walkthrough: Read as E-SCAPE, an online view.
explanation.definitionFit: To get away from something is to elude or evade it.

clue.text: Flower border acceptable in detailed design

indicators.note: one piece goes in another, inside it
de-tailed means losing its tail, the last letter

parts.note: a plan is a design or scheme
a rim is an edge or border
U means upper-class, so socially acceptable

explanation.surface: A flower border features in a gardener's detailed planting design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' reads as 'thorough' but means de-tailed: PLAN loses N.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose and polyanthus belong to this genus of spring-flowering plants.

clue.text: An increasingly conversational relationship

indicators.note: conversational means spoken, so the words are judged by sound

parts.note: an is A and increasingly means more, together a more

explanation.surface: An increasingly chatty relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: A love affair, especially a secret one, is a romantic relationship.

clue.text: Punk band's hit singles

parts.note: to ram something is to strike or hit it
singles are individual units, ones

explanation.surface: A punk band's hit singles.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York group behind 'Blitzkrieg Bop' was a pioneering punk rock band.

clue.text: I will be featured in a poll for wobbly butt of the month

indicators.note: wobbly means unsteady, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Absurd: a wobbly backside is featured in a poll.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes into A POLL FOR, and 'wobbly' rearranges the lot. 'butt' is the target of a joke, not a bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The victim of a 1 April prank is the target of that month's traditional joke.

clue.text: New look given to a foreign currency

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance, as in an air of confidence

explanation.surface: A foreign currency gets a redesigned look.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the monetary unit of Nigeria, so a currency abroad from a British view.

clue.text: One rotten bank

definitions.meaning: a rotten person is a cad or scoundrel
a ship banks or tilts to one side when it ... over

explanation.surface: A single rotten bank.
explanation.definitionFit: It is slang for a dishonourable man, and as a verb a boat leaning over.

clue.text: Australian guards keep it in Worcestershire?

indicators.note: one piece guards another by surrounding it

parts.note: Bruce is the stereotypical Australian man's name in British humour
to own something is to keep or possess it
SA, sex appeal, is crosswordese for it

explanation.surface: An Australian guards something, keeping it in Worcestershire.
explanation.walkthrough: BRUCE is the stock Aussie bloke of British comedy. The question mark marks a definition by example: Worcestershire sauce is a dark brown condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Worcestershire is a dark condiment, an example of the brown savoury relish class.
